title: Acme POS: Refunds & Overrides — Knowledge Check
objectives: Process a refund with manager override in Acme POS
Decide when a manager override is required

items.question: A customer wants a refund but has no receipt. What do you do first?

options.text: Issue the refund right away to keep the customer happy
options.feedback: No-receipt refunds need a manager override — issuing it yourself skips a required control.

options.text: Start the refund and request a manager override when prompted
options.feedback: Correct — the system flags no-receipt refunds for override; start it and call the manager.

options.text: Tell the customer refunds are not possible without a receipt
options.feedback: Refunds are still possible — they just require an override, not a refusal.

items.question: Which situations require a manager override? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A standard refund with a valid receipt, under threshold
Voiding a transaction after the drawer has closed

items.feedback_correct: Right — overrides protect against the higher-risk refund cases.
items.feedback_incorrect: Review which cases carry extra risk — those are the ones needing a manager.

items.question: Why does the POS require a manager override on certain refunds?

options.text: To slow down the line on purpose
options.feedback: It's a control, not a delay tactic.

options.text: To add a second check on higher-risk transactions
options.feedback: Correct — it's a financial control on the riskier cases.

options.text: Because the system can't process them otherwise
options.feedback: The system can process them — the override is a deliberate approval step.
